advances: Ordinary volume for compatible parallel simplex enclosures. The containing-body bound retains its extra volume over the Minkowski sum.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Apply the linear part of an affine map taking $S$ to the standard simplex $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$. This linear change commutes with weighted Minkowski sums for all the stated weights and scales volumes by one common determinant. The image of $S$ is a translate of $T$. In this frame write $a_{ik}=\min_{x\in A_i}x_k$, $b_i=\max_{x\in A_i}\sum_kx_k$ and $r_i=b_i-\sum_k a_{ik}$. Then $A_i\subseteq P_i=a_i+r_iT$, so $r_i>0$ by full dimensionality. Their weighted sum is $(\sum_i\lambda_i a_i)+(\sum_i\lambda_i r_i)T$. The minimum of each coordinate on $K$ and the maximum of their sum are exactly the corresponding weighted sums of the minima and maxima, by separate optimization over the summands. These are the offsets of the simplex $R=\sum_i\lambda_iP_i$. Thus $R$ is supporting on each facet, and equals $S$ if $S$ supports $K$ on every facet.

For ordinary convex bodies, the Minkowski volume polynomial has coefficient for the multi-index $\alpha$ equal to $d!/\prod_i\alpha_i!$ times the mixed volume $V_d(B_1[\alpha_1],\ldots,B_N[\alpha_N])$, with $V_d(B[d])=|B|$. Mixed volumes are monotone in each body argument. These are the standard identities in Schneider, *Convex Bodies: The Brunn–Minkowski Theory*, 2nd ed., §5.1, and in §1.1 of van Handel and Wang. [Schneider, chapter 5](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/convex-bodies-the-brunnminkowski-theory/mixed-volumes-and-related-concepts/C292AF50362C453A9DCD81B43F71A7B6), [van Handel and Wang, On Minkowski's monotonicity problem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.20082).

In the polynomial for the $P_i$ minus the one for the $A_i$, all coefficient differences are nonnegative because $P_i\supseteq A_i$. Retaining only the pure terms of degree $d$ gives $\sum_i\lambda_i^d(|P_i|-|A_i|)\le|R|-|K|$. Zero-weight summands contribute no term. In dimension one every $P_i$ is its own input interval, so the inequality there is immediate. For $R=S$, divide by $|S|=(\sum_i\lambda_i r_i)^d|T|$ to obtain the scale version. If $K=S$, zero total defect forces $|P_i|=|A_i|$ for every positive weight. If some point of $P_i$ were outside $A_i$, strict separation and the cone from that point to an interior ball of $A_i$ would give positive volume in $P_i\setminus A_i$. Thus $A_i=P_i$ at positive weights.

For $K\subseteq Q\subseteq S$, each offset defining $R$ is $h_K(u_j)\le h_S(u_j)$, giving $R\subseteq S$ and the stated slack identity. Minimum enclosures of $K$ or $Q$ exist and have actual facet contacts by a839bfd22b7f11a2.

statement:
Let $A_1,\ldots,A_N$ be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and let $\lambda_i\ge0$ with at least one positive. Put $K=\sum_i\lambda_i A_i$. For an enclosing $d$-simplex $S$ whose every facet supports $K$, use its outward facet normals $u_0,\ldots,u_d$ and set $P_i=\{x:u_j\cdot x\le h_{A_i}(u_j)\ \forall j\}$. Each $P_i$ contains $A_i$ and is a translated positive homothet of $S$, their weighted Minkowski sum is $S$, and
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i^d(|P_i|-|A_i|)\le |S|-|K|.
$$
If $r_i>0$ are the scales of the parallel $P_i$ in any common simplex frame and $\alpha_i=\lambda_i r_i/\sum_j\lambda_jr_j$, this says $\sum_i\alpha_i^d(1-|A_i|/|P_i|)\le1-|K|/|S|$. If $K$ is itself a simplex then each positive-weight $A_i$ is homothetic to $K$.

If $K\subseteq Q$ for a compact convex body $Q$ and $S$ is any enclosing simplex of $Q$, define $P_i$ with the facet normals of $S$ and put $R=\sum_i\lambda_iP_i$. Then $K\subseteq R\subseteq S$ with $R$ supporting $K$ on every facet, and $\sum_i\lambda_i^d(|P_i|-|A_i|)\le |R|-|K|\le (|S|-|Q|)+(|Q|-|K|)$. In particular this holds for every minimum-volume enclosing simplex of $Q$.
title: Transfer of enclosure defects through Minkowski sums
